title: Constrained-Regime Mixed KV vs Whole-Cache Q5
hypothesis_h1: At a real GPU memory-pressure point where whole-cache Q8 cannot provide the desired safe residency but whole-cache Q5 can, a profile-selected mixed Q8/Q5 cache can retain some Q8 layers at the same practical residency and provide better quality than all-Q5.

primary_point_b.product_explicit_q5: succeeds, 32/32 GPU residency, ~68 MiB of the product's own conservative headroom

safe_mixed_q8_boundary.reproduced_from: Phase 11D's own memory_pressure_360m.json boundary, independently reconfirmed fresh in this phase

quality_result.methodology: true F16 ground-truth reference (generated safely at ctx=2048, valid for ctx=180000 candidates because RoPE/KV math depends on real token position, not buffer capacity), 5 pre-registered holdout prompts, gen_tokens=32
quality_result.but: even the best (sensitivity-based) mixed layout is worse than simply staying whole-cache Q5

memory_safety.vram_delta_mixed_vs_q5: 276 MiB measured (nvidia-smi), matches theoretical KV-byte delta (274.66 MiB) to within 1.3 MiB
memory_safety.tighter_empirical_model: predicts mixed top-8 peak to within 0.05%, BUT produces a confirmed FALSE-SAFE result at the real top-8/top-9 boundary -- not safe to productize as-is

control_point_a.confirms_hierarchy: comfortable memory -> Q8, as expected; mixed is not positioned as superior here (not separately re-measured for quality at Point A in this phase -- Phase 11D already established Q8 beats mixed when memory is comfortable)

extreme_point_c.implication: mixed cannot be safer than Q5 here either, since mixed always costs >= Q5 bytes for any Q8 count > 0

future_policy_simulation.note: a mechanical Q8->mixed->Q5->fail hierarchy would fire the mixed branch at Point B, but this phase's own quality data shows that firing would make quality WORSE than falling through to Q5 -- a 'fits' check is not a sufficient gate

authoritative_storage.mechanism: same per-layer ggml_type override mechanism established and repeatedly validated since Phase 11B (patches/llama.cpp-membrane-kv-type-override.patch), reused unchanged in this phase
authoritative_storage.evidence: different --q8-layers sets produce different, config-dependent quality numbers (quality_raw_f16ref.jsonl) -- a shadow/no-op override could not produce config-dependent results; out-of-range/negative layer indices fail closed with exit code 2 (verified live in this phase)

profile_dependency.profile_used: results/phase11/model-specific-policy/profile_360m_train21.json, validated (not regenerated) at the start of this phase
profile_dependency.wrong_or_malformed_profile_fail_closed: established and tested in Phase 11D (cross_model_safety.json), not re-tested from scratch here since the same validated profile/mechanism is reused unchanged
profile_dependency.layer_index_out_of_range_fail_closed: verified live in this phase: exit code 2, clear error, for both an out-of-range (99) and a negative (-1) layer index

limitations: Quality measured on 5 pre-registered prompts, not the full 10-prompt holdout, due to real host RAM constraints on this shared 5.6GiB dev machine (documented in quality_methodology.json before any run)

Point A and Point C were not independently re-measured for quality/naive-layout comparison in this phase (only Point B, the primary constrained point, got the full quality sweep) -- Point A's comfortable-regime quality conclusion leans on Phase 11D's own prior finding

Full sanitizer matrix (llama-free ASan/UBSan, llama-enabled CPU ASan/UBSan, Vulkan Release full product regression across native/q8/q5/adaptive/compare/gpu-bench/auto/guard) was not re-run in full for this phase given real time/host-memory constraints; see regression_sanitizers.json for what was actually run and why

The false-safe finding in overhead_calibration.json means no safety-margin correction from this phase should be treated as productizable without further allocation-time (not steady-state) VRAM instrumentation
decision_gate_rationale: Mixed fits at the same practical residency as Q5 at the primary constrained point, and profile-based (sensitivity) layer placement beats every naive equal-budget layout. But against a true F16 reference, the best mixed configuration is measurably WORSE quality than simply staying whole-cache Q5 (beats Q5 on only 1 of 5 held-out prompts), uses more VRAM, and offers no performance advantage. This does not meet the CONSTRAINED_MIXED_ADVANTAGE_CONFIRMED bar (requires mixed quality measurably BETTER than Q5), and is not fragile/backend-limited/inconclusive -- the measurement was clean, reproducible (deterministic, bit-identical on repeat), and internally cross-validated (VRAM delta matches KV-byte math; F_all_q5 self-check is a perfect sanity control).
next_step_recommendation: Stop mixed-KV productization for the constrained-regime case and retain the product's current whole-cache adaptive policy unchanged. Do not pursue a Q8->mixed->Q5 hierarchy on the strength of this phase's data -- the mixed branch would make quality worse, not better, at the one point measured.
